newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to issue new privatisation vouchers Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to issue new privatisation vouchers Q1 '97.

text.p: Ukraine will issue "communal vouchers" to citizens early next year which they will be able to use to buy shares in state enterprises being sold, the head of the State Property Fund said on Thursday.

"Communal vouchers together with privatisation and compensation certificates will be used by Ukrainians as a method of payment for shares in enterprises at designated auctions," Yuri Yekhanurov told a news conference.
Details will be worked out in January and vouchers will be issued by the end of the first quarter, he said.
He did not say what the value of each coupon would be.
Communal vouchers may also be used to privatise flats, he added.
Each Ukrainian man, woman and child may claim a privatisation certificate, worth about $275 each, until December 31. The deadline for investment is the end of 1997.
About 82 percent of Ukrainians have picked up their privatisation certificates and about 45 percent have invested them.

Compensation certificates were issued to Ukrainians who lost savings as a result of economic changes that happened when Ukraine gained independence in 1991, and are also used to buy shares in enterprises.
